how: Moves read off the chess.com move list in the frames; every move graded by Stockfish 10 (chess-reader.js scoreGame) at depth 16, and the large losses again at depth 20 on one engine. At this depth Stockfish 10's scores vary by about 50 cp between reads of one position, so only losses of 250+ (blunders) are firm; 100-250 (mistakes) are listed as such.
habit: Moving a piece to a square the opponent's pieces already attack or line up on, without checking their captures and checks first: the queen to d3 in line with the e2 knight, the knight to f4 into the bishop's diagonal, and taking back on f4 instead of the free bishop on c4.

losses.happened: After 1.e4 d5 White plays 2.f4, leaving the e4 pawn attacked by d5 and undefended; 2...dxe4 wins it.

factors.position: the e4 pawn attacked by d5 and defended by nothing
factors.information: the opponent's capture dxe4 was the threat

losses.mistake: Not taking or defending the attacked e4 pawn.
unsure: the exact second of the move

losses.happened: With Black's rook on e8 and bishop on e6, White moves the queen from e3 to d3; 16...Bc4 (Stockfish's best for Black) would attack the queen with the e2 knight behind it on the same diagonal, a skewer that wins the knight. Black misses it with 16...Qa6.

factors.position: the queen on d3 and the knight on e2 on one diagonal, open to Bc4; the queen had stood on the e-file in front of the knight

losses.mistake: Putting the queen on d3, in line with the e2 knight on the c4 bishop move's diagonal.
losses.better: 16.d5, gaining space with tempo and keeping the e-file covered.

losses.happened: After the queens come off (17.Qxa6 bxa6), White plays 18.Nf4, onto a square the d6 bishop covers; 18...Bxf4+ wins the knight with check.

factors.position: f4 is on the d6 bishop's diagonal to c1, and nothing of White's defends f4
factors.resources: material: a knight lost for nothing (about -5 by the engine)

losses.mistake: Moving the knight to a square the enemy bishop already attacks, with check behind it.
losses.better: 18.Ng3, or check every square the knight lands on for the opponent's captures.

losses.happened: Down a piece, White attacks the f4 bishop with the rook while the a6 bishop is loose.
Black's 21...Bc4 hangs the bishop to White's a6 bishop; White takes back on f4 instead, and 22...Bxa6 trades off the bishop White could have won.

factors.position: Black's c4 bishop attacked by White's a6 bishop and defended by nothing
factors.information: a free piece on the board

losses.mistake: Recapturing on f4 instead of taking the free bishop.

losses.happened: With Black's rook on e2, White plays 26.Rf1 rather than challenging the e-file.

factors.position: Black's rook on White's second rank

losses.mistake: Not challenging the rook on e2.
